analysis:
The PR is a documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md, with no code, config or policy changes. The head text I received (lines 1-396) covers the date bump at line 3 and the new `addon` subcommand row at head line 156. The base unit (lines 1726-1974) covers the `provider.toml` and environment-variable reference tables, which the file_changes range map shows changed only at head line 1758.

Changed security-relevant content: a new `darkbloom addon` command (debug add-on holds on the running provider: status/hold/release). The patch excerpt says it reaches the provider through the owner-only lifecycle mailbox, bound to the live process identity. Add-ons use a separate local socket documented in addon-hold-ipc.md. This is a new local attack surface: a hold mechanism that could affect provider availability or serving. The threat model has no matching TB or threat for it, and the actual implementation (AddonCommand.swift, the mailbox and the socket) was not supplied.

I cannot verify the socket's authentication, its peer-credential checks, or whether a hold can block serving or drain (a DoS vector for T-010/T-029 style availability). I also cannot verify whether holds interact with App Attest authorization (TB-011) or with the shutdown and update drain paths. The docs describe mailbox access as owner-only, so this is not an observed regression. No finding is warranted from documentation text alone. The next pass should check the add-on hold implementation, the socket permissions and process-identity binding, and whether the threat model needs a new entry for local add-on hold IPC.

The retained base text on prefix cache, SSD, the LaunchAgent environment passthrough, and the App Attest worker flag is unchanged and consistent with T-041 and TB-011. The line-1758 change is not visible in the supplied head excerpt, so I could not assess it.
